matchups.recap: Rob, you got absolutely buttfucked by 1.6 points—that's the fantasy football equivalent of losing a game on a missed extra point, except you did this to yourself by rostering a corpse at running back and praying. You were so close to saving face this week that you could taste it, but instead you're going home with a loss that'll sting every time you check the standings. Adam's sitting here laughing at you with less than 95 points, which tells you everything you need to know about how badly you shit the bed.

Rilind got absolutely dick-slapped by his own blood this week, losing by nearly 20 points to Rinor—and you better believe that's all he's hearing about at every family dinner for the next six months. This wasn't even close; Rilind's team choked harder than a rookie trying to hold a lead in the fourth quarter, while Rinor's squad showed up ready to work. Rinor's gonna be bringing this one up at Christmas, Thanksgiving, and probably just random Sundays when he feels like reminding Rilind what it means to actually know how to build a roster. Better luck next year, little bro—or maybe just don't show up to family functions until you can put some fucking points on the board.

Jetmir and Peter got absolutely cock-blocked by five points—like showing up to a party thinking you're gonna run the place and instead watching from the corner nursing a warm beer. You had every chance to steal this one and still managed to piss it away, which tracks perfectly with your season of catastrophic decision-making. Flamur didn't even have to play that well; your dumpster fire of a roster just imploded on its own. Better luck next week, I guess—though we both know that's not happening.

Ilir got absolutely buttfucked by a 9.3 point margin this week—which is impressive considering he had a full roster of actual NFL players and still managed to leave points all over the goddamn field. His team played like they were being paid to lose, and honestly at this point Arben could've started a waiver wire scrub at flex and still won this one. Better luck next week, you fantasy football dumpster fire.

Nori got absolutely throttled by 5.4 points and somehow that's still being generous—his roster played like it was actively trying to tank the season. With a measly 73.9 points, he managed to field a lineup that looked like it was assembled during a blackout at a dive bar. Faton's 79.3 wasn't exactly lighting the world on fire either, but in a battle between two mediocre rosters, Nori's incompetence just barely edged out the competition.

Veton got absolutely skull-fucked this week, losing by 24.2 points like he forgot he was supposed to actually set a fucking lineup. Ben rolled out his team like a functional adult while Veton apparently thought benching his studs and starting a parade of backups was some kind of 4D chess move—spoiler alert, it wasn't. This wasn't even a matchup, it was a mercy killing dressed up as a fantasy football game.

matchups.preview: Rinor's pulling into this matchup with a pulse and actual wins under his belt, while Rob's sitting at 0-2 looking like he drafted exclusively from the "I heard this guy was good in 2019" bin. This is Rob's chance to finally put points on the board, but let's be honest—his roster has all the consistency of a hamstring injury report, and Rinor's just hungry enough to make sure Rob's 0-3 dreams come true this week.

Adam's already half-cocked at 1-1 while Flamur's sitting pretty at 2-0, which means this is exactly the week Adam's dumbass roster decides to finally show up—right before collapsing spectacularly in Week 4 like always. Flamur's probably going to get cute with his lineup and bench his best player for some waiver-wire lottery ticket, but even his self-sabotage won't be enough to save Adam from another L. Lock in that third loss, buddy—your draft picks are already writing the obituary.

Rilind's sitting at 1-1 trying to figure out how to not completely implode, and now he's gotta face a 2-0 squad that's actually got their shit together? This is the week Rilind's season either stabilizes or goes full dumpster fire—and honestly, with the way his roster's been limping along, Arben's about to make him regret every questionable start he's made so far.

Asllani and Mardjonovic are sitting at 1-1 with absolutely zero consistency, looking like they're managing by dartboard while Kastrati's somehow clinging to .500 despite whatever dumpster fire roster decisions got them here. This week, the question isn't who wins—it's whether either of these teams can string together two competent weeks in a row without imploding spectacularly.

Ilir Asllani vs Ben Vucetaj, both sitting at 1-1 and desperately trying to convince themselves they know what they're doing—this is basically a Battle Royale of mediocrity where one of you gets to feel slightly less incompetent for a week. Asllani's got just enough wins to think he's in this thing, but we all know that's just variance before the wheels fall off; Vucetaj's in the same boat, floating on the last remnants of draft day delusion. One of you clowns is about to get exposed this week, and honestly, it could go either way because you're both running about as smooth as a rusty shopping cart.

Faton limps in at 1-1 like he's barely holding on by his fingernails, while Veton's sitting at 0-2 looking like he's already checked out for the season. This is a battle between a guy who can't string together wins and a guy who can't win period—basically watching two dumpster fires argue about whose garbage smells worse. Faton's got the edge in experience at losing, so he should take this one by default.
